Blue Ridge Family Office.title: Blue Ridge Family Office - SSO go-live slipped past the sold date: Root cause analysis
Blue Ridge Family Office.markdown:
# Blue Ridge Family Office - Root Cause Analysis: Technical Report

## What Failed and Why
- Two distinct test failures occurred during the implementation process:
  1. Role claim mismatch: The platform mapped user roles from a 'roles' claim, whereas Okta sent data under 'groups', causing users to land with no role assigned.
  2. Missing JIT provisioning: New users attempting to log in were not created automatically, resulting in a 403 error because JIT user provisioning is not supported on this tenant tier and was not included in the implementation scope.
- Scoping handoff gap: The initial scoping call notes did not mention JIT provisioning, so Mai Le's standard rollout plan never included it. Tom Becker put down the October date based on instinct without checking with implementation.

## How it was Detected
- Discovered through customer test windows on Sep 18 (role claim mismatch) and Sep 25 (JIT provisioning 403 error).

## What was Contained and Fixed
- Metadata configuration: Done.
- Claim mapping: Resolved.
- JIT provisioning: Moved to engineering development.

## Open Questions
- Exact design review outcome date: not recorded

# Root Cause Analysis: iOS Safari E-Sign Bug

## What Failed and Why
- The signature pad failed and became completely unresponsive on iOS Safari when the page was zoomed in.
- Root cause involved touch-event coordinate mapping issues when the viewport was scaled.

## Detection
- Discovered during pre-release testing and reported by Lê Thu Hà for six investors attempting to sign on mobile devices.

- Engineering investigated touch-event coordinate mapping.
- Minh Tran verified touch-event offset fix on safari mobile; logs confirmed `touch_move_scale_corrected` for test signatures.
- Hotfix deployed and ticket moved to Done.

- Hana promised a 5pm Thursday release without specifying a time zone.
- Customer understood Vietnam time, while the release went out Pacific time (7am Friday Vietnam), causing a missed signing slot.

## Overview
- Customer: Granite Bay Infrastructure
- Case: Silent sync failure to the fund administrator (Northstar)
- Status: Active escalation regarding an SLA breach and silent pipeline drop.

## Incident Summary
The nightly sync to Northstar failed starting October 6 due to an SFTP key rotation. The failure went unnoticed for 10 days because automated alerts were routed to a retired mailbox, and the customer was ultimately notified by Northstar rather than Anduin.

## Impact

# Root Cause Analysis: Granite Bay Infrastructure Northstar Sync Failure

## Incident Description
The nightly data sync of investor commitments and capital accounts to Northstar Fund Services over SFTP failed silently following an SFTP key rotation. Authentication was rejected by the remote server every night starting October 6.

## Root Cause
- Expired or rotated SFTP key.
- Monitoring alerts were misconfigured and routed to a retired mailbox (data-sync-alerts@) instead of the active on-call channel.
- Compounding factor: Weekly log review missed the auth failures because Jake Morales was on leave for two weeks.

## Detection
The issue was not detected internally. Priya Raman from Northstar notified Granite Bay after noticing balance mismatches for the upcoming quarter-end reporting.

## Containment and Fix
- Missing nightly files were backfilled for all affected dates and acknowledged by Northstar.
- A tracking item was created for monitoring updates to ensure alerts page the on-call engineer directly.
- Other customers with the same sync setup were checked; their connections remain active.

## Open Questions
- What specific date was the retired mailbox decommissioned? Not recorded.

# Lessons Learned: Granite Bay Infrastructure Retrospective

## What Went Well
- Once identified, engineering acted quickly to verify error logs, confirm the scope across other customers, and successfully backfill all missing records for Northstar.
- Cross-functional communication via Slack and Jira enabled rapid coordination between engineering, support, and customer success teams.

## What Did Not Go Well
- Automated alerts failed because they were routed to a retired mailbox, resulting in a 10-day silent failure.
- Weekly log reviews failed to catch the authentication errors due to staff leave coverage gaps.
- A clear SLA breach occurred because the customer learned of the failure from a third party (Northstar) rather than Anduin within the 4-hour notification window.

## Follow-ups and Owners
- Deliver the formal RCA by Monday, October 19 (Owner: Rebecca Stone).
- Implement direct paging for the on-call engineer for all data sync failures (Owner: Alex Duong / Engineering).

title: KYC verification runbook
markdown:
# KYC verification runbook

## How investor verification works
- Limited partners submit their accreditation and identification details during the digital subscription process.
- Anduin initiates KYC/AML verification through an integrated vendor.

## The vendor hand-off
- Investor data is transmitted securely to the vendor for screening.
- The vendor returns status updates, matching flags, or requests for additional documentation via API webhooks.

## What to check when LPs are stuck in pending
- Check the vendor dashboard for unverified identity flags or mismatched data.
- Verify if the investor needs to upload clearer identification documents.
- Confirm whether manual review has been triggered on the vendor side.
- If the issue persists, review webhook logs for delivery failures between Anduin and the vendor.

- Severity 2 and 3: Not recorded.

- Maintain transparency regarding platform availability and expected resolution times.
